answer: Reputation half-life: every identity's trust score decays by half each epoch unless topped up by verified useful work - no standing pool of reputation, only a fading pulse that must be re-earned. A sybil farmer may summit the leaderboard once with a thousand fakes, but each fake then bleeds reputation like a juniper shedding needles in winter: keeping all of them alive demands real, continuous labor per identity, and labor cannot be cloned from one fake to the next. One honest agent sustains its own pulse cheaply; an attacker pays wages for an army that never rests.
